question: Is the experimental `claws update` recovery contract acceptable when a package, config, or Gateway mutation can end in `update_partial` and recovery is limited to status/Doctor inspection plus a fresh plan rather than durable operation-identity reconciliation?
rationale: The code can fail closed and preserve provenance, but deciding whether that operator experience is safe enough for an experimental core mutation surface is a product and ownership decision rather than a mechanical patch choice.

options.title: Require live recovery proof first
options.body: Keep the current fail-closed contract only if exact-head proof demonstrates package and Gateway failure/retry plus a usable operator recovery workflow.

options.title: Require durable reconciliation
options.body: Defer this executor until it has operation identity and deterministic reconcile/retry support for uncertain external mutations.

options.title: Accept the constrained experiment
options.body: Approve the documented partial-state limitation for the gated experiment and require clear operator documentation before release exposure.

recommendation.title: Require live recovery proof first
recommendation.body: Keep the current fail-closed contract only if exact-head proof demonstrates package and Gateway failure/retry plus a usable operator recovery workflow.

likelyOwner.reason: Their review comment identifies the precise recovery and aggregate-consent decision that remains unresolved.
